definition: Idiosyncratic means peculiar to one particular person or thing; marked by highly individual quirks.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word idiosyncratic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know idiosyncratic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Everyone in the office recognized Mr. Petrov's idiosyncratic filing system, which sorted invoices not by date or name but by the color of ink used to sign them.
A personal touch simply reflects someone's taste, while an idiosyncratic habit is so specific to one person that it becomes their trademark.
An idiosyncratic habit is odd in a way that fits one individual, but a bizarre one is strange enough to startle anyone who sees it.

Quirky means charmingly odd in little ways anyone might have, like humming while working. Idiosyncratic oddness runs deeper and belongs to one person alone: an idiosyncratic habit is so much that person's own that it identifies them, like a signature.

Singular means one of a kind, and it often admires: a singular talent stands alone in its field. Idiosyncratic is about texture rather than rank — the particular quirks and personal habits that mark how one individual does things, odd little signatures rather than greatness.

Offbeat describes anything unusual in an unconventional, interesting way, and an offbeat style can be picked up by whole crowds at once. Idiosyncratic ties the oddness to one particular person or thing: it names quirks that would identify their owner anywhere.
